analysis:
I found no security regressions in this batch, so there are no findings. All changes are CI or doc-only: .github/workflows/ci.yml (head text only, no patch supplied), the new .github/workflows/dev-deploy-safety.yml, and an AGENTS.md patch. The batch contains no coordinator, provider or attestation runtime code, so TB-002, TB-009, TB-011, T-052..T-058 and T-041 are not touched by any runtime path. The workflow files are not part of the production runtime threat model; the GitHub Actions/R2 release supply chain is declared out of scope.

dev-deploy-safety.yml (new): it triggers on push to master/main and on pull_request, not pull_request_target. It sets permissions to contents: read and persist-credentials: false, and uses a SHA-pinned checkout. It runs scripts/run-dev-deploy-safety-ci.sh with the constant matrix.platform values 'Ubuntu 24.04' and 'macOS 27', so there is no expression injection (lines 26-51). It declares no secrets. The runner script and scripts/test-dev-deploy.py are not in the diff, so their contents are not reviewed. The workflow header comment says deploy-dev.yml arrives with PR 1370, and that workflow is also not reviewed.

ci.yml: the actions are SHA-pinned. I saw no pull_request_target usage and no secrets exposed to PR code. The release-integrity job adds offline tests, including scripts/test-app-attest-entitlements.py (line 43) and the threat-review test scripts (lines 52-56). Coordinator and provider tests run at lines 105-125 and 300-313. I could not verify what the tests assert. ci.yml has no top-level permissions block, but I cannot tell from head text alone whether that is new, and the job-level permissions for 'changes' are set.

AGENTS.md: only the repo-layout text changes, to mention deploy/gcp/dev/swap.sh. This has no security effect. Later passes should check deploy/gcp/dev/*, scripts/run-dev-deploy-safety-ci.sh and any deploy-dev.yml for credential or prod/dev boundary handling, if those files appear in other units.
